decision_reason: NASA/JPL's 2015 NPO-49266 technical-support-package page describes CASH as a reusable XML-configured framework that uses LDAP groups to customize Cassini team pages and links to this exact repository. The public repository contains source and a standard Apache-2.0 license, first committed with the code on 2013-12-31. However, the repository has only five commits ending in 2013, and no current product-specific use, support, or distribution evidence was found; the historical 2015 TSP does not establish a current maintained/operational product. Hold pending a current exact-product use/support signal and verified installation/user guidance.

government_provenance.note: NASA Tech Briefs' exact NPO-49266 record says the framework was done by Andrew P. Darwin and Delvison Castillo of Caltech for NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and links to the reviewed NASA GitHub repo.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the PHP/XML website framework source, README, sample assets and readme.pdf without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository root LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0. Its first observed license-bearing code commit is https://github.com/nasa/cash/commit/c5965d7801f47904eabe4801bbd396de0c92333e (2013-12-31). NASA Tech Briefs separately says commercial licensing is available for the NASA technology; no contradictory restriction on the Apache-licensed repository code was found.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA/JPL TSP documents the exact framework and its intended use, but it dates to 2015. No current, product-specific deployment, support, or distribution signal was found for this 2013-quiet repository, and the source README itself provides little operational guidance.

decision_reason: This is NASA Johnson Space Center's CFS Command and Data Dictionary utility, a reusable ground tool for editing spacecraft command/telemetry definitions and producing files for flight/display systems. NASA's software catalog identifies the exact product and links to this repository; a NASA Technical Reports Server paper documents CCDD being chosen and successfully used to automate/autocode Habulous spacecraft software. The current CCDD-2 branch has versioned 2.1.13 release notes, install/developer/user guides and a tutorial, plus substantive source activity through June 2026. Its LICENSES.md applies NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 to CCDD, an OSI-approved license. The first branch grant-bearing LICENSES.md commit was 2017-08-03.

government_provenance.note: NASA's catalog entry MSC-26167-1 specifically names the CFS Command and Data Dictionary Tool, describes its ground-based spacecraft-data role, and directs users to https://github.com/nasa/CCDD. NASA NTRS identifies the CCDD tool in JSC's Habulous project paper.

public_source.note: The public CCDD-2 branch exposes Java source, packaged jar, build scripts, installation/developer/user guides and tutorial. Branch activity includes substantive commits through 2026-06-30.

eligible_license.note: The branch license file explicitly assigns NASA Open Source Software Agreement v1.3 to CCDD; NASA says NOSA is OSI-approved and OSI lists NASA-1.3. The license-bearing commit is https://github.com/nasa/CCDD/commit/b6c8f2293f11e338a018813552dd29b9cfaf8359 (2017-08-03). The Javadoc subtree contains its own bundled third-party license texts, which do not replace the NASA-1.3 grant for CCDD-authored application source.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA JSC paper says the CCDD tool was selected to manage the Habulous command/data dictionary and successfully used to automate/autocode flight software. NASA's product catalog and the current branch README provide product-specific release, setup, and user guidance.

decision_reason: NASA Langley's exact CertWare Safety Case Workbench release and source repository are public, and the main CertWare software is released under NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3. But the license text explicitly excludes bundled third-party libraries from that grant; it says some are Apache-2.0 while SamIam is licensed only for educational/research non-commercial use. Because this repository distributes an integrated Eclipse workbench with those libraries and product-wide commercial/open-source scope is not resolved, hold pending a clear separable product/license boundary. NASA's current catalog page also calls this old unsupported code, and repository source activity ends in 2016.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact LAR-18067-1 software page names CertWare Safety Case Workbench Software and its Download Now link resolves to https://github.com/nasa/CertWare. The repo's embedded NOSA file identifies NASA and NASA Langley Research Center.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the Eclipse workbench plugin source, documentation, build metadata and embedded library plugins without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The actual grant says NASA OSA 1.3 covers CertWare excluding listed third-party libraries, and specifically says the SamIam library is for educational/research non-commercial use only; other bundled libraries include Apache-2.0. The integrated product-wide scope is therefore not shown to be uniformly OSI-compatible. Resolve exact separability/scope before treating the repository as an eligible product.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's current software page identifies the exact workbench, explains its safety-case model-processing role and links its repository; it explicitly warns that the code is older and unsupported. README describes Eclipse plugins/editors and NASA distributes a LAR-numbered release, but this evidence does not clear the mixed library-license scope.

decision_reason: This is the distinct NASA Goddard CFDP (CCSDS File Delivery Protocol) cFS application, not the cFE core or the cFS umbrella bundle. NASA's current Goddard cFS catalog directly links to this app and says it transmits files to/receives files from the ground; NASA's Software Catalog identifies version 2 (GSC-16125-1), and the archived SourceForge source release dated 2015-03-13 redirects users to this exact current repository. The active dev branch has substantive source updates through 2026-09-24, a standard Apache-2.0 root license, and application user-guide generation instructions; the broader cFS repository provides build/execution guidance.

government_provenance.note: NASA Goddard's current cFS catalog lists the CCSDS File Delivery Protocol App (CF), links to the exact nasa/CF repository, and describes its ground file-transfer function. NASA Software Catalog GSC-16125-1 separately identifies the CFDP Version 2 release as Open Source.

public_source.note: The active public dev branch contains C implementation, tests, configuration, CMake/build files and documentation; latest substantive commits are dated 2026-09-24.

eligible_license.note: The actual current root LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0 for the CF application repository. It was added in commit https://github.com/nasa/CF/commit/1ec62f5a35ce348897e3efe20c914bb1a4cbd2cd (2022-03-14). The exact NASA GSC-16125-1 product release was already publicly listed as open-source source on 2015-03-13; NASA identifies NOSA v1.3 as its OSI-approved release agreement. The present reviewed code is directly covered by Apache-2.0.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's exact GSC-16125-1 page describes CFDP transmit/receive behavior and its NASA Software Catalog Download Now source route; the NASA Goddard cFS catalog maps this app to the current GitHub repo. Its versioned product record and application guide/build documentation establish a reusable standard-protocol implementation, not merely a test or example component.

decision_reason: This is the NASA Goddard Core Flight Executive (cFE), a distinct core component of the cFS—not the umbrella bundle or a cFS application. The direct SourceForge archive shows a versioned cFE 6.1.1 source release dated 2012-01-20 and its README states the source is under the NASA Open Source Agreement; NASA's own open-source page confirms NOSA is OSI-approved. The current GitHub default dev branch carries Apache-2.0, has substantive updates through 2026-09-25, and is directly linked by NASA's GSC-18128-1 Version 6.7 software page and current Goddard cFS material. The public cFE user guide and cFS bundle's build/execution instructions support user installation/use; NASA reports the cFS platform has powered 40+ missions.

government_provenance.note: NASA's GSC-18128-1 software page identifies Core Flight Executive version 6.7, describes cFE services and directly links Download Now to the reviewed GitHub repository. NASA Goddard's current cFS pages identify cFE as a core framework component.

public_source.note: The public default dev branch contains cFE framework code, tests, CMake/build tooling and a detailed user's guide; current source activity includes a commit on 2026-09-25. The README links the integrated cFS bundle's build and execution instructions.

eligible_license.note: The current root LICENSE is the standard Apache License 2.0. The earliest verified public licensed-source snapshot is NASA's cFE-6.1.1-OSS-release-3 (2012-01-20), whose bundled release README explicitly states NASA Open Source Agreement; NASA confirms NOSA v1.3 is OSI-approved. The current source is directly covered by Apache-2.0.

primary_evidence.note: NASA Goddard identifies cFE as the core component providing scheduling, inter-process communication and error management for the reusable cFS, which it says has supported 40+ NASA missions. NASA's current product page is versioned and directs users to source; the repository and cFS bundle include user/build documentation.
